column2: Those among the Arjika tribes, among the active ones, those among the dwellers, or among the five peoples.
May those, the sounding divine drops, flow for us rain from heaven and heroic strength.
For you are everywhere alike, lord over all quarters; we call you in battles.
In battles we call on Agni for help, desiring strength — wondrous in bounty in contests.
For you are our father, O Vasu; you, hundred-powered, have been our mother; so we ask your favor.
I speak to you, O strong, much-invoked, strength-seeking, born of might; give us heroic strength.
Whatever you think choice, Indra, heavenly, bring that; may we know that bounty of yours, the unfailing giver.
By that famed great mind of yours, accomplished in every direction, O stone-bearer, you break even the firm to win strength.
They cleanse the newborn desirable child; the Maruts adorn the sage with their troop; the seer with songs and poetry, the seer, Soma, passes through the filter roaring.
The sage-minded, who makes sages, gaining heaven, of a thousand guides, the leader of the seers; the great one, desiring the third realm, Soma, rules after Viraj, the Stubh.
The falcon, sitting in the vessel, the bird, the all-bearing, cow-finder, drop, bearing weapons; joining the wave of the waters, the great one speaks to the sea, the fourth realm.
These somas have flowed toward Indra's dear desire, increasing his heroic strength.
Purified, sitting in the vessels, going to Vayu and the Ashvins — bestow on us heroic strength.
For Indra's bounty, Soma, flowing, urge on the heart; sit in the seat of the gods.
The ten fingers cleanse you, the seven thoughts urge you on; the sages have rejoiced after you.
For the gods, for exhilaration, you are released across the wool; we clothe you with cows.
Purified in the vessels, the ruddy bay one guards the cattle-treasures with garments.
Flow for us to the bounteous; drive away all enemies; O drop, enter as a friend.
We would enjoy you, Indra-drunk, man-watching, finder of heaven, with offspring and food.
Flow the rain of heaven and splendor upon the earth; set strength in us in battles, Soma.
Soma purifying flows, thousand-streamed, across the wool, to the appointed place of Vayu and Indra.
Seeking help, sing to the sage who is flowing, who is pressed for the gods' feast.
The somas flow for the winning of strength, of a thousandfold vigor, praised for the gods' feast.
And flow for us for the winning of strength, great nourishment, O drop, splendid heroic vigor.
They have been released like swift mares urged on by the drivers, for the winning of strength, the swift ones to the woolen sieve.
May those pressed divine drops flow to us a thousandfold wealth and heroic strength.
The longing drops flow toward their calf like mothers; they have been held in the hands.
Pleasing to Indra, the exhilaration, flowing, roaring, drive away all enemies.
Smiting the niggards, flowing, seeing heaven — sit in the seat of truth.
The somas, the drops, have been released, pressed with the stream of truth, most honeyed for Indra.
The sages sang toward Indra like milch-cows to their calf, to drink the soma.
The exhilaration-dropping, wise wave of the river sits in the seat; Soma is lodged on the cow-skin.
The navel of heaven, the all-seeing, is honored in the woolen sieve — Soma, the skilful seer.
The soma that is placed in the vessels, within the filter — the drop has embraced it all around.
The drop drives speech on the ridge of the ocean, urging the honey-dripping vessel.
The lord of the forest, ever praised, among the cow that gives milk, urging the human work.
Flowing one, bring wealth of a thousand splendors; for us, O drop, a self-existing one.
The sage of heaven, the wise, is pressed with the stream toward the dear ones; Soma, I urge far away.
Your strengths rise like the sound of the river wave; urge the arrow's flow.
At your impulse three speeches rise up, the sacrifice-seeking ones, when you go to the woolen height.
They urge the dear bay one with the woolen sieves with stones, the flowing honey-dropping one.
Flow to us, most exhilarating, through the filter with the stream, seer; sit in the seat of the hymn.
Flow, most exhilarating, anointed with cows and nights; enter Indra's belly.
Then at once he broke the forts for Divodasa, Shambara — and then that Turvasha, Yadu. [Next:] Flow around us, O drop, wealth of horses, cattle and gold; stream a thousandfold nourishments.
Bring us great wealth, flowing one; drive away foes; give heroic fame, O drop.
Not a hundred nor the crooked ones diminish your bounty, when, purified, you are for the sacrifice.
The Sun yoked his horse Etasha, the flowing one, over Manu, to travel through the air.
And the Sun yoked those bay mares for the journey; the drop is Indra, so they say.
Make Agni, with fires, the god, together-minded, the best sacrificer, a messenger at the rite — who among mortals is steadfast, true, hot-headed, ghee-fed, pure.
Like a horse eager for fodder, when he stands out of the great enclosure, then the wind follows his flame, and then your path is black.
When, O Agni, the new-born bull's ageless flames rise, you go to heaven, ruddy, with smoke; you are sent as messenger to the gods.
Indra is made for giving, the most powerful, set in strength, splendid, praised, the soma-drinker.
Like a thunderbolt gathered by song, mighty, unshaken, fierce, unconquered, he carries.
O Adhvaryu, bring the soma pressed by stones to the filter; purify it for Indra's drinking.
Those gods, O drop, have attained your honey-drink, the Maruts of the flowing one.
Press for Indra the thunderbolt-bearer the best nectar of heaven, the most honeyed soma.
The upholder of heaven flows, the skilful essence, the skill of the gods, to be rejoiced in by men; the bay one, released like a horse among the strong, you vainly make strength in the rivers.
Like a hero he takes weapons in his hands, desiring heaven, a charioteer seeking cattle; urging Indra's strength with the workers, the drop is urged and anointed by the wise.
O Soma of Indra, flowing with a wave, strong, enter his belly; swell heaven and earth for us like lightning in the cloud; with thought bring us everlasting strengths.
Indra, when you are called by men from east, west, north and south, from many places — you are the mighty protector of Anu, Turvasha, praised for strength.
Or when among the Rumas, Rushamas, Shyavaka, in the Krupa, Indra, you rejoice together; the Kanvas, with hymns and prayer-driven, hold you; come, Indra.
Him indeed, the self-ruler, the bull, the two cups shaped with might; and you sit first of equals, for your mind longs for soma.
Flowing one, you stir wealth, praiseworthy Soma; O drop, enter the sea.
We, O Vasu of every Vasu, much-desired, would be nearest to your nourishments, in your favor, unconquerable.
The sounding exhilaration-dropping drop flows around in the woolen sieve; the stream that rises at the sacrifice goes like light, desiring cattle.
Bright, flow for the gods, Soma, for heaven and earth, and bless the offspring.
You are the upholder of heaven, bright nectar; in the true rite, racer, flow.
I praise your dearest guest, beloved like a friend — Agni, who is to be known like a chariot.
Like a seer to be praised, whom the gods in two ways have placed among mortals.
You, youngest, protect the men of the giver; hear our songs; guard our offspring and ourselves.
You are truly, soma-drinker, over both worlds; you are Indra, strengthener of the presser, lord of heaven.
You, Indra, are the upholder of the eternal forts; slayer of the Dasyu, strengthener of Manu, lord of heaven.
You uncovered the cave of Vala, rich in cattle, O stone-bearer; the gods, fearless, urged by you, came forward.
They have praised Indra the ruler with hymns, by might; whose gifts are a thousand, or even more.
Rejoice, O Vayu, for worship and bounty; rejoice Mitra and Varuna, as you are purified; rejoice the Marut host; rejoice the gods; rejoice heaven and earth, god Soma.
This immortal god is given like a leaf-bird, to sit in the troughs.
This god, praised by the sages, plunges into the waters, giving jewels to the giver.
This one seeks all desirable things like a hero with his troops, flowing.
This god drives like a charioteer, flowing, he reveals the way.
This god is cleansed by the wise, truth-loving, the bay one, for strength.
This god made by the sage runs over crookednesses, flowing, unconquerable.
This one runs through heaven with the stream across the spaces, flowing, roaring.
This one has spread over heaven across the spaces, untouched, flowing, of good sacrifice.
This one of many vows, being born, begetting nourishments, flows pressed with the stream.
This hero goes with thought, swift with his chariots, going to the appointed place of Indra.
This one goes with many thoughts for the great worship of the gods, where the immortals have reached.
The Ayus cleanse this cleansable one in the troughs, who brings great nourishments.
This one is set and led along the pure path, when the swift ones hurry.
This racer is driven with golden bright rays, becoming lord of the rivers.
This herd-bull shakes his horns, sharpens them, holding manly power by might.
This one, drinking the treasures, passes beyond the hard places; he goes down into the stalks.
This bay one the ten fingers urge on to go, well-armed, most exhilarating.
This bull-chariot has been cleansed through the woolen sieves, going to a thousandfold strength.
The women of Trita urge this bay one with stones, the drop for Indra to drink.
This one sits among the human clans like a falcon, going like a lover to his beloved.
This exhilarating essence looks down, the child of heaven, the drop that entered the woolen sieve.
This one is pressed for drinking; the bay sustainer runs, roaring to his dear nest.
This one the ten bay mares, the workers, adorn, by which he is decorated for exhilaration.
This racer is set by men, all-knowing, lord of the mind; he runs to the woolen sieve.
This soma has flowed in the filter, pressed for the gods, entering all abodes.
This god shines in his nest, immortal, Vritra-slayer, best at the gods' feast.
This bull roared, held by the ten sisters, runs to the vessels.
This one made the sun shine, flowing in the sky; in the filter, the exhilarating drink.
This one is shining with the sun, together with Vivasvat, the unconquerable lord of speech.
This seer is praised and urged in the filter, purifying, smiting enemies.
This one, heaven-winner, is poured round for Indra and Vayu, in the filter, accomplisher of skill.
This pressed bull, head of heaven, is led by men — Soma in the woods, all-knowing.
This cattle-loving, gold-loving flowing drop has roared, the always-victorious, unconquered.
This strong bull, the bay one, ran in the air; the purified drop to Indra.
This strong, unconquerable Soma flows purifying, guardian of the gods, slayer of the evil-speaking.
